findings.explanation: The add-on assigns every event the sourcetype `cisco:ucs` and encodes the class in `source` (`cisco:ucs:lsServer`, `cisco:ucs:faultInst`, and so on). The text also tells readers to prefer these non-existent sourcetypes 'per Splunkbase 2731 field guidance', which is the opposite of what the add-on documentation says.
findings.quote: the sourcetypes `cisco:ucs:inventory` (XML inventory MO snapshots; you filter `classId="lsServer"` for the Service Profile object), `cisco:ucs:audit` (UCSM audit-style lifecycle and operator actions on the same MO classes), and `cisco:ucs:faults`
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the feeds as `sourcetype=cisco:ucs` with `source=cisco:ucs:lsServer`, `source=cisco:ucs:faultInst` and, for audit, the source for the UCSM audit class (for example `aaaModLR`) once a Template includes it. Remove the claim that `cisco:ucs:inventory`/`cisco:ucs:audit` are the shipped names.

findings.explanation: The add-on documentation installs to `$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/Splunk_TA_cisco-ucs/` and Splunkbase lists the package as `Splunk_TA_cisco-ucs`. The hyphen is the canonical name, not a quirk.
findings.quote: The on-disk directory name and canonical app id use an underscore. Older local packages may still list a hyphen in the filename; that is a packaging quirk
findings.suggested_fix: State that the app folder and id are `Splunk_TA_cisco-ucs`. Cite the current 4.3.3 release and its compatibility range.

findings.explanation: The add-on has no separate inventory, audit and faults inputs. You add a Manager (host and credentials), build Templates listing class IDs (for example lsServer, faultInst, aaaModLR), and create Inputs that reference `servers` and `templates`, with default sourcetype `cisco:ucs`. Following Step 1 as written would not produce the data the search expects.
findings.quote: enable the modular inputs the vendor documents for inventory poller, audit log (or audit-equivalent) pull, and faults; bind each to `index = cisco_ucs` (or your standard name) and keep the sourcetype the TA assigns (`cisco:ucs:inventory`, `cisco:ucs:audit`, `cisco:ucs:faults`). A representative pattern is to copy the stanza names from `default/inputs.conf` ... fill `url = https://<ucsm-fqdn>`
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite Step 1 around Managers, Templates and Inputs as documented. Validate with `index=cisco_ucs sourcetype=cisco:ucs | stats count by source`.

findings.explanation: The companion search's `rex` has no named capture group. Splunk's rex command requires at least one, so the search errors out instead of returning the cause histogram.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the rex line (the following `where match(...)` already filters to profile DNs) or give it a named group, for example `(?<sp_key>org-root/(?:.+/)?ls-[^/]+)`.

findings.explanation: UCSM audit records (`aaaModLR`) usually carry attributes such as `affected`, `ind` (creation/modification/deletion), `descr`, `user`, `txId` and `cause`, not a result or outcome field. If so, `audit_fail` never evaluates to 1 and half the detection is dead.
findings.quote: `audit_fail` encodes: audit side red conditions—HTTP-like failure tokens in the normalized `result` field, profile DNs, and action verbs for associate, modify, decommission, or disassociate
findings.suggested_fix: Pull one real audit event from the add-on and list its attributes. Then describe the audit branch in terms of the fields that actually exist, or state that association failures are detected from lsServer state and faultInst only.

findings.explanation: `inaccessible` is documented as a fault (fltLsServerInaccessible) and an operational condition. It may not be a value of lsServer `assocState`, whose usual values are associated, associating, disassociating, failed and unassociated.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the lsServer assocState and operState enums in the UCSM MIM. If `inaccessible` belongs to operState, document it there.

findings.explanation: This introduces yet another sourcetype that neither the add-on nor the subcategory guide defines.
findings.quote: add a `join` to `cisco:ucs:events` in a private fork if your site indexes FSM there
findings.suggested_fix: Name the actual source for FSM data (for example a class such as `lsServer` FSM children captured via a Template) or remove the suggestion.

findings.explanation: The text never names the Cisco fault that represents this condition, which would make validation and alerting concrete.
findings.quote: Open the Faults summary for the same profile and read the `cause` and severity
findings.suggested_fix: Name the relevant UCSM faults from the Cisco faults reference (fltLsServerAssociationFailed, fltLsServerConfigFailure, fltLsServerInaccessible) and their codes, verified against the reference.

findings.explanation: The Server Management Guide reference points to the Cisco home path, and the Splunk reference points to the Search Reference index rather than a specific page.
findings.suggested_fix: Link the actual UCSM Server Management Guide chapter on service profiles and the specific Search Reference pages used (eval, rex, join).

findings.explanation: A UC with non-existent sourcetypes and a companion search that does not run cannot have been verified against a live deployment.
findings.suggested_fix: Set a non-verified status until validated.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: The search filters `sourcetype="cisco:ucs:inventory"`, `sourcetype="cisco:ucs:audit"` and `sourcetype="cisco:ucs:faults"`. The Splunk Add-on for Cisco UCS emits `sourcetype=cisco:ucs` with class-specific `source` values (for example `cisco:ucs:lsServer`, `cisco:ucs:faultInst`), so the search returns nothing on a default install.

The fault join regex `^(?<sp_key>org-root/.*?/ls-[^/]+)` requires a sub-org segment between `org-root/` and `/ls-`, so faults on service profiles in the root org (`org-root/ls-NAME/fault-...`), the most common layout, never join and `cause_enum` stays empty. Use `^(?<sp_key>org-root/(?:.+?/)?ls-[^/]+)`.

`first(inv_fail)`/`first(audit_fail)` take an arbitrary row per sp_dn rather than any failing row (use `max`). `latest(assoc)` and similar fields can be overwritten by empty strings from audit rows. The joined `fault_sev` and `fault_time` are computed but never shown in the final table.

summary: The UC explains the association-failure idea and its blast-radius logic well, but it is built on three sourcetypes the Splunk Add-on for Cisco UCS does not emit. It also gives an inputs.conf workflow that does not match the add-on, ships a companion search that fails as written, and keys the audit branch on fields UCSM audit records may not have.
